column1: # Allowances for scripts/doc_gates.sh GATE 47 (`code-needles`): registered retracted phrasings
# that a NON-markdown tracked text file legitimately contains. GATE 3 scans *.md and
# reports/evidence/**; every other tracked text file (solve.c, verify.c, *.py, *.sh, *.lean,
# *.tsv, *.json, ...) is GATE 47's corpus, and the SAME registry (RETRACTED_PHRASES.tsv) is its
# needle set. GATE 3's allow COLUMN does not apply here — it is filename-scoped and was written
# for the markdown ledger; a code file needs a row in THIS table instead.
# WHY A SEPARATE TABLE, AND WHY THIS SHAPE. A phrase legitimately survives in code for exactly two
# reasons: (a) a CORRECTED block quotes the withdrawn wording in order to withdraw it (solve.c's
# header, verify.c's and tests.py's WHAT-WAS-WRONG comments), and (b) the gate scripts hold the
# needles themselves in their own comments (doc_gates.sh, corrections_inventory.sh). Neither is a
# reason to exempt a FILE: a second, live use of the same phrase in the same file is exactly the
# defect this gate exists to catch (solve.c:19 carried one fifteen lines below the block that
# withdrew it). So every row names the FILE, the PHRASE (byte-identical to its registry row), and
# the MAXIMUM occurrence count measured when the row was written. More occurrences than `max`
# FAILS; ZERO occurrences FAILS too — a stale allowance is a row that could later hide a new use,
# and it is reported by name rather than tolerated. Widening a row is a one-line edit that the
# gate prints on every run.
# Columns (tab-separated): file <TAB> phrase <TAB> max <TAB> anchor <TAB> reason
#   anchor = one or more fixed strings separated by `|`; EVERY allowed occurrence must be preceded,
#   within 170 characters of the folded+flattened file, by one of them. This is the withdrawal
#   CONSTRUCTION (`This read`, `once gave`, `WHAT WAS WRONG`, the gate's own `fixed string` fixture),
#   and it is what separates a quote-to-withdraw from a live use — a bare count cannot: the pre-fix
#   solve.c (ff804bb0^) held the Q-353 phrase exactly ONCE (the live :19 site) and the fixed file holds
#   it exactly once too (the quote that withdraws it). Measured 2026-09-02; the count-only first cut
#   passed the pre-fix tree, which is why this column exists.
# Measured 2026-09-02 (code-fix lane), each count from the same fold+flatten pipeline GATE 3 uses.
